## 1. Central Bank held the Overnight Policy Rate at 8.75% as inflation drifted above target and external risks stayed elevated.

Policymakers noted <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">headline prices rose 6.8% year-on-year in June</span> and projected a gradual return to the 5% objective. They signalled vigilance over demand conditions while stating that May’s tightening would continue to filter through credit and spending.

Officials highlighted a recent <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">current account deficit since April</span> alongside higher fuel import costs and softer tourism earnings. <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Gross reserves stood at $6.45 billion</span> at end‑June, while the currency stabilised in recent weeks after earlier policy measures.

The Board cited <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">renewed Middle East tensions</span> and global commodity moves as upside risks to prices. It reaffirmed readiness to act to keep inflation anchored around the target and support medium‑term growth.

## 2. Brent crude briefly crossed $100 a barrel, reviving cost and external pressures.

The benchmark price touched a two‑month high after <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Red Sea tanker incidents</span> and later eased but remained elevated. A sustained rise would lift <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">import bills</span> and could widen trade gaps if tourism receipts and remittances do not offset higher energy outlays.

Domestic <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">price pass‑throughs to transport</span> and LPG have historically raised living costs. The central bank flagged the oil move as a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">risk to its near‑term price path</span> in its latest review.

## 3. Japan sought interest on delayed compensation for the cancelled Colombo LRT project.

Authorities confirmed three payments were made in 2024—<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">JPY 189.7 million</span> on 23 August, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">US$ 1.031 million</span> on 27 August, and Rs. 108.7 million on 24 September. Tokyo later <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">requested interest</span>, and a committee is now reviewing the claim.

Cabinet <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">terminated the rail scheme on 24 September 2020</span> after officials deemed it not cost‑effective. The move has left residual financial issues with contractors and consultants that remain under examination.

## 4. Health authorities capped lab charges during the dengue surge as clinicians urged early care over vaccination.

Regulators reminded private providers that a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Full Blood Count with report must not exceed Rs. 400</span> and the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">NS1 antigen test Rs. 1,200</span>. Complaints can be lodged via the 1977 hotline with receipts for enforcement.

Clinicians reported <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">78,125 infections</span> and 56 deaths so far this year, with <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">162 MOH areas at high risk</span>. Specialists advised immediate treatment for warning signs and said a vaccine is not a solution to the current wave.

## 5. Government set out plans to lift the renewable share above the current 70% target and reinforce the grid.

Officials said they would upgrade the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Sampur–Kappalthurai line from 300 MW to 600 MW</span> and construct <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">four additional transmission systems</span>. The President also called for investment in a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Northern 400 kV</span> (kilovolt, a unit of electric potential) backbone to carry more variable power.

## 6. President ordered tighter protection of fast‑developing coasts and faster delivery of human‑elephant conflict projects.

A steering committee will oversee coastline works, with an expert panel tasked to report on <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">erosion at Oluvil</span>. The Environment Ministry reviewed a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 19,719 million portfolio</span> and was told to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">finish funded mitigation projects within the year</span>.

## 7. Fisheries agencies mapped 2027 priorities and relief after Cyclone Ditwah.

Sector leaders reviewed harbour upgrades at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Myliddy, Gandara and Rekawa</span> and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">rehabilitation at Karainagar</span>. A <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 189 million programme</span> to replace boats and nets for affected families is underway alongside plans to raise exports and local supply.

## 8. Police probed the abduction and killing of a foreign national after a clash at a waterfront development.

Investigators recovered a body hidden under stones in <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Karandana, Eheliyagoda</span>, and seized a vehicle believed to have moved the victim. <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Two suspects were arrested at the airport</span> while attempting to depart, and consular officials <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">requested a full inquiry</span>.

## 9. A new daily rail service will connect the capital with Thalaimannar Port.

<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Train No. 5003</span> will leave at 03:50 and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">arrive at 10:44</span>, with the return, No. 5004, departing at 04:10. The rake will serve major Northern Line stations and offer <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">two air‑conditioned first‑class coaches</span> with reserved seating.

## 10. The national passport rose to 94th in the 2026 Henley Index.

The ranking <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">improved from 96th in 2025 and 2024</span>, compared with 100th in 2023 and 102nd in 2022. The index rates travel documents by <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">visa‑free and visa‑on‑arrival access</span> across <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">227 destinations</span> (a methodology that counts entry without prior permits).
